15 An electric motor produces 120 W of useful mechanical output power. The efficiency of the motor
is 60%.
Which row is correct?
waste heat power
electrical power
input / W
output / W
A
72
48
B
192
72
C
200
72
D
200
80

hints: Notice the 120 W is the useful mechanical output power, while the electrical power in the table is the total input power, so input must be greater than 120 W.
Recall efficiency for power as $efficiency = useful\ output\ power / input\ power$, so with 60% efficiency rearrange to $input\ power = 120 \text{ W} / 0.60$.
Connect input and waste by conservation of energy: $input\ power = useful\ output\ power + waste\ heat\ power$, so subtract 120 W from your input to get waste.
walkthrough: Identify the given quantities: useful output power $P_{useful} = 120 \text{ W}$ and efficiency $= 60\% = 0.60$.
State the governing rule: $efficiency = P_{useful} / P_{input}$ for steady power flows.
Use energy conservation for power: $P_{input} = P_{useful} + P_{waste}$, so $P_{waste} = P_{input} - P_{useful}$.
Calculate waste: $P_{waste} = 200 \text{ W} - 120 \text{ W} = 80 \text{ W}$. The row with 200 W input and 80 W waste is option D. This is option D.

A.explanation: 72 W is $0.60 \times 120 \text{ W}$, which treats 120 W as the input. The 120 W is the useful output, so input must be larger than 120 W.

B.explanation: 192 W input would give efficiency $120/192 = 0.625$. It incorrectly adds 72 W to 120 W instead of using the 60% relation correctly.

C.explanation: 200 W input is correct but 72 W waste is wrong. Waste is not 60% of the useful power and is not $200 - 128$.

D.explanation: Input $= 120/0.60 = 200 \text{ W}$ and waste $= 200 - 120 = 80 \text{ W}$, matching 60% efficiency.
